summary: Lanterns on movable masts guided boats into Covehead Harbour from 1879; today's wooden tower, built 1975 after a 1967 predecessor, stands in the national park dunes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register entry says the present tower was built in 1975, replacing a 1967 structure; sources giving 1967 or 1976 as the first or tower year refer to the earlier tower or are imprecise. Range lights on masts date from 1879.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: no NRHP-style nomination, no newspapers searched, no Canadian Parks statement (the DFHD page returned only a placeholder). Lighthouse Friends says Lloyd Bell kept the range lights 1926-1959 in prose but 1936-1959 in its keeper list; the story uses the list. Kielly's appointment: LF gives 1900-1911, Marine reports 1890 at Cove Head (Inner/Range light); keeper table matched by position in OCR. The 1893 report text is quoted via Lighthouse Friends, not read directly. The 1967 tower's location (French Wikipedia says Red Point) is unsourced and omitted. The coveheadlighthouse.com domain now serves spam and was not used. Whether the Friends group acquired the lighthouse is unknown. Only the 1975 build year and 1967 predecessor come from the register; Lighthouse Directory 1976 unverified. Fact-check 2026-10-27: 1918 moveable-lights work matched to Covehead by position (Covehead is first station in the list, $46.08 first amount; page image not viewed). Tower colour: register says white with red trim, CCG says white with red upper portion. Focal height: CCG 11.0 m vs Lighthouse Friends 10 m.
